verificationTransitionPreserved.beforeFix: The classifier only matched `npm test`/named runners, so a direct `node paginate.test.js` run derived NO test receipt; brief.verification was EMPTY and the HTML read 'No verification receipt captured' despite a real failed->passed test run in toolEvents. This was a genuine product defect surfaced by S2 dogfooding.
verificationTransitionPreserved.fix: Broadened RECEIPT_CLASSIFIERS test regex to also match a direct execution of a file following a test/spec naming convention (`*.test.*`/`*.spec.*` in js/ts/py/rb/go). Still conservative — a plain `node server.js` does NOT match. Regression test added (both the failed and passed run become receipts; `node server.js` yields none).
verificationTransitionPreserved.afterFix: brief.verification has 2 entries; the failing run is honestly status:unknown ('the receipt does not prove a successful exit') carrying the AssertionError, the passing run is status:observed ('All tests passed.'). No fabricated exit code.

honestLimits: Proves a real LOCAL debugging session (reproduce->diagnose->fix->verify) flows unchanged through 1B synthesis into a self-consistent, tamper-evident local explanation whose Verification panel preserves the failed->passed transition. Does NOT prove remote publication or externally-signed authenticity (out of scope; publication is always local_only).

The failing test run is honestly status:unknown, not 'failed-then-fixed' as a single fabricated claim — the transcript records tool_result is_error but not a process exit code, so no exit code is invented.

The classifier broadening is conservative: it fires only on a filename that itself signals a test/spec (`*.test.*`/`*.spec.*`); a normal `node server.js`/`python app.py` run is still NOT a verification receipt. A test run via an unconventional filename would still be missed (acceptable false-negative bias — we never fabricate a receipt).
S3 multi-session is recorded as the next OPTIONAL step and does NOT block the single-session path; it is deferred until after the context-blind >=90% gate.
The context-blind 8-question evaluation is the remaining acceptance gate (#6) before final GO.
